account: Today has appeared mostly quiet. I followed my market walk, lunch, and accounts appointments and am now at the neighbour's dockside cottage for three o'clock tea. Several townspeople independently repeated that the baker was carrying wheat at the bakery. The neighbour likewise repeatedly mentioned the baker making fresh bread, and now says the baker described it as simply his usual baking. That repetition catches my attention, but wheat and fresh bread are normal bakery business, and I have not witnessed anything improper. The secretary reports no correspondence, financial submissions, or requests requiring decisions. Both office books were returned to their chest. The most unusual remark is the neighbour's unsolicited statement that there are no confirmed new riverside projects: I had asked about dockside gatherings and visitors, not projects. This might reflect an informal proposal or local discussion, but it could also be an innocent conversational remark. I have just asked what prompted it and what residents want for the quarter. So far, I cannot identify any hidden undertaking, its participants, or its purpose. The baker and neighbour are possible sources of further information, not established participants in anything suspicious.
